paper.title: Contextual Bandit Algorithms with Supervised Learning Guarantees

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial contextual bandit / K-armed bandit with expert advice
unmapped: Experts give probability-vector advice over arms; regret measured against expected return of best expert
settings.definition_quote: On each round $t$, the world commits to $\rr(t) \in [0,1]^K$. Then the $N$ experts make their recommendations $\bxi^1(t), \ldots, \bxi^N(t)$, and the learning algorithm $\Alg$ (seeing the recommendations but not the rewards) chooses action $j_t\in \{1,\ldots,K\}$. Finally, the world reveals reward $r_{j_t}(t)$ to the learner

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic contextual bandit competing with a policy class of finite VC dimension
unmapped: Possibly infinite policy class with VC dimension d_VC, known to the learner
contexts and rewards drawn i.i.d. from a fixed unknown joint distribution D
settings.definition_quote: A standard VC-argument in the online setting can be used to apply Exp4.P to compete with an infinite set of policies $\Pi$ with a finite VC dimension $d$, when the data is drawn independently from a fixed, unknown distribution. For simplicity, this section assumes that there are only two actions ($K=2$)

conditions: the set of experts includes one which selects an action uniformly at random on each round

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Assume that $\ln(N/\delta) \leq KT$, and that the set of experts includes one which, on each round, selects an action uniformly at random. Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, \[G_{\ExpP} \geq G_{\max} - 6\sqrt{KT \ln(N/\delta)}.\]

results.notes: G_max is the (expected-over-advice) return of the best expert. Runtime is O(NK) per round (polynomial in N); paper notes inefficiency for very large N.

symbols.d_VC: VC dimension of the policy class Pi

conditions: contexts and rewards drawn i.i.d. from a fixed distribution D
tuning: tau = sqrt(T(2d ln(eT/d) + ln(2/delta))) uniform exploration rounds

source.label: thm:VC
source.quote: For all distributions $D$ over contexts and rewards, for all sets of policies $\Pi$ with VC dimension $d$, with probability $1-\delta$, \[ G_{\textrm{VE}} \geq G_{\max(\Pi)} - 9\sqrt{2T \left(d \ln \frac{eT}{d} +\ln \frac{2}{\delta} \right) }. \]

results.notes: Exp4.P runs over up to (e tau/d)^d representative policies, so computation may be exponential in d; not stated.
